page.layout: One page of text, with a running head at top left ("De Deo.") and a centred running title "Liber 1." under the page number "2". Main text in one column with marginal references at right (Exo/Rom, Num/Cor, Philip, and a bracket-marked note column). Diagram-like braces in the middle of the page (Sic autem manifesta-ta est vel ...). Right edge shows show-through and a catchword-like "Est" at lower right.

main_text.l: Gloria Dei est ipsius excellentia supra omnia
Ea est gloriæ divinæ manifestatio qua ipsa Dei
σχῆ-μα (ut fieri & ferri possit) sensibus communicatur:
quæ communicatio, præsentiæ ipsius & gloriæ divinæ
rior est apertius ipsius similitudinem sive προσ-
ωπον, & tanquam os ad os ipsum intueri. Ibid.
Dan.7.10. Mat. 18. 10. quæ semper & præcipue in
tertio cœlo, id est, supremo cœlo manifestatur. Psal.
Obscura magis, quæ fit ænigmatibus tanquam
Inuisibilis est, quæ intellectui per cognitionis me-
Sic autem manifesta-ta est vel Ipsius θειότης.
Θειότης est ipsius Dei essentia vel natura. Ibid.
Θειοτέλος attributum, quod Deo ad ipsum ma-
gis nobis declarandum vere attribuitur. Ibid.

page.notes: Two printed pages on the scan: the left page is the main text; the right edge shows show-through and a partial second page, not transcribed. The diagram with braces (Sic autem manifestata est vel...) is rendered approximately; Greek words and some marginal reference marks are doubtful. Greek forms such as σχῆμα and προσωπον are uncertain readings.
